item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 270509
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Mon Oct 26 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located a few hundred miles south-southwest of
Manzanillo, Mexico, and has issued the last advisory on
Post-Tropical Cyclone Olana, located several hundred miles
west-southwest of Johnston Atoll.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Tue Oct 27 2026 
325 
WTPZ32 KNHC 270848
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
200 AM MST Tue Oct 27 2026
 
...VANCE WEAKENS SLIGHTLY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.9N 106.9W
ABOUT 275 MI...440 KM SW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 320 MI...515 KM SSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern and west-central coasts of Mexico
and the southern Baja California Peninsula should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 15.9 North, longitude 106.9 West. Vance is
moving toward the northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h). A northwestward
motion is expected to continue today, followed by a gradual turn
northward on Wednesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is expected during the next day or so,
followed by gradual weakening.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 200 miles (325 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4
inches of rain across central and southern Sinaloa, western Durango,
and coastal sections of Nayarit and Jalisco, with isolated higher
totals of 7 inches possible over Sinaloa. This rainfall may produce
flooding and mudslides, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect portions of the coast of
southern, southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Tue Oct 27 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 270849
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
200 AM MST Tue Oct 27 2026
 
Vance's satellite presentation has continued to deteriorate
overnight. Satellite imagery reveals a fully exposed low-level cloud
swirl that continues to become increasingly separated from the deep
convection to its southeast, with the nearest convection now
displaced over 100 n mi from the center. A 0411 UTC Metop-B
scatterometer pass sampled a small area of 45-kt winds within the
displaced convection, while winds closer to the center were
generally 30 to 35 kt. Given the increasingly disorganized structure
of the cyclone and recent objective intensity estimates ranging from
35 to 45 kt, the initial intensity is lowered to a possibly generous
40 kt.
 
The initial motion is northwestward, or 310/7 kt. This general
motion should continue today as Vance is steered by a weakening
mid-level ridge to its north. Falling heights aloft associated with
a series of shortwave troughs rotating through a broad mid- to
upper-level trough over the West Coast of the United States should
then cause the cyclone to gradually turn north-northwestward during
the next 12 to 24 h, northward between 24 and 36 h, and
north-northeastward thereafter. The latest NHC track forecast is
very similar to the previous prediction, but has been nudged
slightly westward toward the latest HCCA and GDMI aids.
 
Strong westerly to southwesterly vertical wind shear is expected to
persist and increase during the next several days as Vance gradually
moves northward. Despite warm sea surface temperatures, the
combination of increasing shear and relatively dry mid-level air
should continue to inhibit organized deep convection near the
center. Although some fluctuations in strength are possible,
intermittent convective bursts could help maintain Vance's intensity
during the next day or so before a gradual weakening trend begins.
Global model guidance generally supports this scenario, depicting
convection remaining displaced well east of the circulation. Vance
is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low in about 60 h,
although this transition could occur sooner if organized deep
convection fails to redevelop near the center. The latest NHC
intensity forecast is similar to the previous prediction, with only
minor adjustments, and lies near the middle of the guidance
envelope.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact
portions of western Mexico during much of this week. This rainfall
may produce flooding and mudslides across central and southern
Sinaloa, western Durango, and coastal sections of Nayarit and
Jalisco, especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
2. Interests along the southwestern and west-central coasts of
Mexico and the southern Baja California Peninsula should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  27/0900Z 15.9N 106.9W   40 KT  45 MPH
 12H  27/1800Z 17.0N 107.8W   40 KT  45 MPH
 24H  28/0600Z 18.6N 108.4W   40 KT  45 MPH
 36H  28/1800Z 20.2N 108.6W   35 KT  40 MPH
 48H  29/0600Z 21.7N 108.5W   35 KT  40 MPH

$$
Forecaster Gibbs
